t: #2274 Maximum Consecutive Floors Without Special Floors
o: Rented floors span [bottom, top]; special floors split this range into gaps of ordinary floors. Return the largest gap length. Example 1: specials {4,6} split [2,9] into lengths 2, 1, 3 → answer 3. Example 2: every floor is special → 0. Since top can be 10^9, we cannot mark floors individually; sorting the special floors and measuring gaps between neighbors (plus the edges) is the way.
k: Sort the special floors; the answer is the max of: first special − bottom, top − last special, and consecutive specials differing by more than 1 contribute (diff − 1).
Never materialize the floor range — only O(S) values matter.

a.i: After sorting, walk through the special floors tracking the previous special (initialized to bottom − 1). Each consecutive pair contributes prev_gap = cur − prev − 1 ordinary floors; also account for the tail top − last. Take the maximum.
s: For each s in special: ans = max(ans, s − prev − 1); prev = s.
a.t: O(S log S) — sorting the special floors dominates; the scan is linear.

w: One clean approach suffices here. Pitfalls: forgetting the leading gap (bottom to first special) and trailing gap (last special to top) — initializing prev = bottom − 1 and doing a final max with top − prev handles both uniformly. The formula s − prev − 1 correctly yields 0 for adjacent specials. Follow-up: streaming specials too large to sort — external sort or a heap-based selection of the maximum gap.
